question:
A 27-year-old man with a history of intravenous drug use comes to the physician because of anorexia, nausea, dark urine, and abdominal pain for 2 weeks. Physical examination shows scleral icterus and right upper quadrant tenderness. Serum studies show:
Alanine aminotransferase 1248 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase 980 U/L
Hepatitis B surface antigen negative
Anti-hepatitis B surface antibody positive
Anti-hepatitis C antibody negative
Further evaluation shows hepatitis C virus RNA detected by PCR. Without appropriate treatment, which of the following is the most likely outcome of this patient's current condition?"?
analysis: The patient has acute hepatitis C infection, as indicated by the presence of hepatitis C virus RNA despite negative anti-hepatitis C antibodies. In many cases, acute hepatitis C can resolve spontaneously without treatment, leading to a transient infection. However, if left untreated, a significant proportion of patients may develop chronic hepatitis C, which can progress to liver cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma over time. Given the acute nature of the symptoms and the current findings, the most likely outcome without treatment is a transient infection, as many individuals clear the virus spontaneously within 6 months.
